# Style 02 · Swiss Precision

> Clarity built on a visible grid.

**Keywords:** Objective · Rational · Structured · Confident · Direct  
**Mood:** Trustworthy · Minimal · Technical  
**Sectors:** Finance & professional services · Real estate · Education & public sector · Technology & SaaS  
**Strongest applications:** Presentations · Print & editorial · Websites · Brand identity · Advertising

> **Fictional sample brand.** Brandt Okafor Advisory, strategy and finance consultancy, and every person, figure and address in its examples are invented to demonstrate this style. This is not client work. Domains use the reserved `.example` TLD.

## Concept

Based on the International Typographic Style, Swiss Precision gets its authority from order. A strict modular grid, one grotesk family, flush-left text and a single signal red make complex information look under control. Numbers and data are treated as design elements.

## Target industries

- Consulting and advisory
- Banking and fintech (B2B)
- Law firms
- Architecture and engineering
- Annual reports and investor relations
- Industrial and manufacturing

## Color palette

| Name | Hex | Role | Share |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| Paper | `#FFFFFF` | Primary background | 62% |
| Ink | `#111111` | Text, rules, data | 24% |
| Concrete | `#E9E9E7` | Panels, table stripes | 8% |
| Graphite | `#5C5C5C` | Secondary text | 3% |
| Signal Red | `#E2231A` | Accent: one key number or action | 3% |

**Rule:** Use Signal Red once per layout, on the single most important number, word or action.

## Typography

| Role | Family | Weights | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display | **Instrument Sans** | 500, 700 | Headlines, large figures |
| Body | **Instrument Sans** | 400, 500 | Body copy, tables, navigation |
| Utility | **IBM Plex Mono** | 400 | Figures, footnotes, reference codes |
| Arabic | **IBM Plex Sans Arabic** | | Matches the neutral grotesk tone. Align Arabic to the right edge of the same grid columns. |

**Type scale** (desktop, px size / line height)

| Level | Size | Weight | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display | 88 / 88 | 700 | -3% tracking, sentence case |
| H1 | 48 / 52 | 700 | -2% tracking |
| H2 | 24 / 30 | 500 | Sentence case |
| Body | 16 / 24 | 400 | Flush left, ragged right |
| Caption | 12 / 16 | 400 | Mono for figures and sources |

- Use one type family with no more than two weights per layout.
- Set text flush left and ragged right. Never justify or centre.
- Show hierarchy through size and position, not colour.

## Layout rules

- **Grid:** 12 columns · 24px gutter · baseline grid of 8px
- **Spacing:** 8px base. Modules snap to 4 × 8px rows.
- **Corners:** 0 everywhere.

- Show the grid: use 1px rules on column lines to structure content.
- Hang headlines from the top-left of their module.
- Use asymmetry: text in 5 columns, white space in 7.
- Number sections and figures (1.0, 1.1) for reference documents.
- Use oversized numerals as visual anchors.

## Photography direction

Documentary architecture and people at work, cropped hard to the grid.

- Architectural lines, stairs and facades, shot straight on.
- People in real workplaces, candid, mid-task.
- Crop images to exact grid modules, never free-floating.
- Use black and white with red as the only colour cue where possible.
- Neutral, even daylight.

**Sample shot list**

1. Concrete stairwell, symmetrical, straight on (grade: `#D6D6D4` → `#9A9A98` → `#3A3A3A`)
2. Partner at whiteboard, candid, b/w (grade: `#EDEDED` → `#8C8C8C` → `#1C1C1C`)
3. Glass facade grid, overcast sky (grade: `#C9CDD1` → `#7E858C` → `#2B2F33`)

**Avoid**

- Stock handshakes and staged meetings
- Tilted or dramatic angles
- Warm colour grading

## Graphic elements

- Visible column rules and grid crosses
- The red square: a solid block used as a section marker
- Oversized figures and percentages
- Simple data charts in ink with one red series
- Section numbers in mono (01.2)

## UI examples

- Rectangular buttons in Ink. Red only for the main action on a page.
- Inputs are boxed with a 1px Ink border and a label above.
- Tables use Concrete stripes and mono figures.
- Focus states are a 2px red outline.

- Primary button: `Request a proposal` · Secondary button: `Read the report`
- Input: Company: `Northbridge Holdings`
- Tags: `Strategy` `M&A` `Risk`
- Card: **Market outlook 2027**, Report 04.2 · 36 pages, +18.4% CAGR

## Social media examples

- Lead with one number or one statement per post.
- Carousels follow a numbered sequence, same grid on every slide.
- LinkedIn first. Keep the style consistent with reports.

| Format | Eyebrow | Headline | CTA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Feed post 1080 × 1080 | Insight 04 | 62% of mid-market deals stall at due diligence. |  |
| Story 1080 × 1920 | Report 04.2 | Market outlook 2027 | Download |
| Feed ad 1080 × 1350 | Advisory | Decisions, backed by data. | Book a call |

## Website example

- Hero is typographic: a large statement plus one key figure.
- Use a visible 12-column grid across all pages.
- Case studies lead with the result number.

- **Navigation:** Services · Insights · Team · Contact
- **Hero eyebrow:** Strategy · Finance · Transactions
- **Hero headline:** Clear advice for complex decisions.
- **Hero copy:** We help leadership teams price risk, plan growth and close transactions with confidence.
- **Actions:** Request a proposal / Our insights
- **Proof row:** 120+ (Transactions advised since 2011) · 14 (Markets across Europe and the Gulf) · 4.1bn (Deal value under advisory in 2026)

## Advertising campaign

**Campaign:** Numbers First

Every execution leads with one verified figure from the firm's own research, with the source printed underneath.

| Format | Eyebrow | Headline | CTA |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Billboard 48-sheet (6096 × 3048 mm) | Brandt Okafor Advisory | 62% of deals stall at due diligence. | boa.example/insight-04 |
| Display MPU 300 × 250 and leaderboard 728 × 90 | | Market outlook 2027. 36 pages. | Download |

- Every figure carries its source in mono below it.
- Book airport, business-district and financial-press placements, plus LinkedIn.
- The red square sits in the same corner in every format.

## Presentations

- **Cover slide:** Report 04.2 · **Market outlook 2027** · Board briefing · sample deck
- **Content slide:** 2.1 Where deals stall. Key figure **62%** (stall at due diligence); points: Data room not ready: 41%; Valuation gap: 33%; Regulatory review: 26%. Figures are sample data.

- Number slides and sections (2.1, 2.2) so the deck can be cited in meetings.
- The slide title states the conclusion, not the topic.
- One red data point per chart.

## Brand applications

Business card, letterhead and email signature for **Daniel Okafor**, Managing Partner (`d.okafor@boa.example`, fictional).

| Application | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| Reports | A4, 12-column grid, mono figure captions |
| Signage | black letters on white walls, red square as floor marker |
| Email signature | name, title, one red square, no image logos |
| Proposal covers | title at 88pt, report number in mono |

- The logo is a word plus the red square. Never redraw it in another colour.
- Templates (Word, PowerPoint) are part of the identity. Ship them with the logo.
- Keep one weight change per document level.

## Do / Don't

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Align everything to the grid | Centred text blocks |
| Let numbers carry the message | Decorative illustrations |
| Keep one colour accent | More than one font family |

## Design tokens

Text in the accent colour uses `--avdl-accent-text`, which passes WCAG AA (4.5:1) on both `bg` and `surface`.

```css
[data-style="swiss-precision"] {
  --avdl-bg: #FFFFFF;
  --avdl-surface: #F3F3F1;
  --avdl-ink: #111111;
  --avdl-muted: #5C5C5C;
  --avdl-accent: #E2231A;
  --avdl-accent-text: #C41E16;
  --avdl-accent-2: #111111;
  --avdl-on-accent: #FFFFFF;
  --avdl-line: #111111;
  --avdl-font-display: 'Instrument Sans', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif;
  --avdl-font-body: 'Instrument Sans', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif;
  --avdl-display-weight: 700;
  --avdl-display-case: none;
  --avdl-display-tracking: -0.03em;
  --avdl-radius: 0px;
  --avdl-button-radius: 0px;
  --avdl-border-width: 1px;
  --avdl-shadow: none;
  --avdl-color-paper: #FFFFFF;
  --avdl-color-ink: #111111;
  --avdl-color-concrete: #E9E9E7;
  --avdl-color-graphite: #5C5C5C;
  --avdl-color-signal-red: #E2231A;
}
```
